title: Recoil transport and environmental exposure of black-hole merger remnants
abstract: Black-hole mergers in stellar clusters leave remnants whose recoil carries them through environments of different density and composition. Their availability for subsequent interactions depends on residence in those environments, as well as on gravitational retention. We study when continuous drift and diffusion preserve finite-time residence under discrete gravitational encounters. Published multimass distributions for six Galactic clusters supply consistent potentials, species distributions and local scattering backgrounds. Collisionless controls connect these inputs to orbital occupation, while a conditional Omega Centauri calculation compares finite encounters with diffusion having the same local velocity-change moments. A backward occupation equation relates their mean-residence difference to a nonlocal generator residual. We test a first-response approximation through complete-transition replacements, recording predictions before independently sampled mixture validation. Symmetric covariance-root coupling substantially improves response-estimator precision. An independent test with that coupling nevertheless leaves endpoint prediction accuracy unresolved, with rare scores dominating the estimated variance. Resolution sensitivity and population bounds on residence beyond numerical termination remain separate limitations. The calculations identify distinct requirements for an observable-specific transport criterion: resolving the response, controlling numerical refinement, and bounding continuation of stopped histories. They establish conditional encounter effects and a more precise method for testing their residence response, without claiming calibrated cluster residence or merger rates.
